""" result = tabulate([], headers=["A", "B"], tablefmt="simple") # Expected simple format with headers only: no leading spaces before the separator line. expected = normalize("A B\n--- ---") assert normalize(result) == expected # Helper to count occurrences of a substring in the output def count_substring(s, sub): return s.count(sub) def test_tabulate__missingval_and_thousands(): # Missing value handling and thousands separator parsing (lines 1371‑1385) data = [["spam", None, "1,234"], ["eggs", 42, "5,678"]] out = tabulate(data, headers=["A", "B", "C"], missingval="?", tablefmt="simple") # Missing value should be replaced by "?" assert "?" in out # Numbers with commas should be displayed unchanged (since they are not parsed as numbers) assert "1,234" in out and "5,678" in out def test_tabulate__prepend_row_index_error(): # Provide a showindex iterable of wrong length to trigger ValueError (line 1436) data = [["x"], ["y"]] with pytest.raises(ValueError): tabulate(data, showindex=[0, 1, 2], tablefmt="simple") def test_tabulate__header_multiline_align(): # Header with newline triggers align_header multiline path (lines 1393‑1408) out = tabulate([[1, 2]], headers=["Col\nOne", "ColTwo"], tablefmt="simple") # The header line should contain both parts separated by a newline in the output assert "Col" in out and "One" in out # Ensure that alignment does not raise and the table renders assert "1" in out and "2" in out def test_tabulate__ansi_and_color_and_strip(): # ANSI colored number should appear (the library does not strip ANSI codes by default) red_number = "\x1b[31m123\x1b[0m" out = tabulate([[red_number]], tablefmt="simple") # The output should contain the plain number and the ANSI escape sequences assert "123" in out assert "\x1b[31m" in out # In simple format there is a separator line of dashes;
